evidence: src/controllers/cardsController.ts: create, activate, getStatement, blockCard, unblockCard, createVirtual each destructure the request and delegate to cardServices.* before res.send/sendStatus
src/controllers/paymentsController.ts: buyOnPointOfSale and buyOnline delegate to paymentServices.insertPayment / insertOnlinePayment and respond with sendStatus(200)
src/controllers/rechargeController.ts: recharge delegates to rechargeService.recharge and responds with sendStatus(200)
Only paymentsController.ts declares typed request-body interfaces (BuyOnPOSBody, BuyOnlineBody); the other controllers use untyped req.body, a minor style inconsistency
No file duplicates validation or business invariants; none accesses repositories directly
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files in src/controllers serve one concern: thin Express handlers that pull values from the request, delegate to the matching service (cardServices, paymentServices, rechargeService) and send an HTTP status or payload. No business rule or invariant is repeated across files, since validation and domain logic live in the services. No handler bypasses the service abstraction to reach persistence directly. One minor inconsistency: only paymentsController gives its request bodies types (BuyOnPOSBody, BuyOnlineBody), while cardsController and rechargeController read req.body untyped. This is a style difference, not a split concern or a duplicated rule. paymentServices and onlinePaymentSchema import these body interfaces from the controller, but that is an import-direction issue and out of scope here.
